text: A matrix version and a masking version resolve at sign-in and stay until the session ends, so open work keeps the version it signed in under and a new version answers only new sessions.
why: The legacy flow step 5 keeps open sessions on their version and RWB-E1-022 resolves the version at sign-in; no source states the rule for the split service.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-037 section 4 step 5; FSD P4 A2.4; RWB-P4-E1022-APP
confirm: Solution architect with the access owner
impact: A withdrawn permission stays in force for the life of an open session, up to the session timeout; the alternative is a per-request resolve, which costs one read per call.

text: A person whose roles include both halves of a role_conflict row at the conflict version in force is refused the session, and the refusal is recorded with reason ROLE_CONFLICT.
why: The separation-of-duty rule is in the legacy story and the sources give no other enforcement point; the session is the earliest point at which the pair can be seen.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-019 BR9 and section 10; FSD P4 AC-EXC-P4-001-03; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 role_conflict
applied_in: RWB-P4-E1037-APP sections 2 and 9; RWB-P4-E1037-CON sections 8 and 9
impact: A mistaken entitlement blocks the person at sign-in instead of being discovered in an audit, and the incident queue carries the pair.

text: An Entra ID group that maps to no Workbench role, or to an inactive role, gives the person no role at all and no default.
why: Default deny is the architecture rule and no source defines a fallback role; a fallback would grant rights nobody approved.
read: Architecture v5 slides 10 and 35; legacy MSG-P4-001
impact: A person with one unmapped group of several keeps the roles of the mapped groups and is refused 401 only when no group maps.

text: rwb-access caches no data of another service and no answer of a peer: the version in force is read from rwb_access on each call, and only the platform library caches the policy answer in the consuming service.
why: P4 owns the policy rows, so a local cache adds a staleness window with no gain, and the sources give no cache to the access owner.
read: Architecture v5 slide 20 (cache in the consuming service); slide 14 (rwb-access is the reference-data owner)
impact: Each read costs one query on rwb_access inside the 2 s budget; a policy change is visible to a new session at once.

text: The access log is written locally through the decision-record library to rwb.decision-record.v1 and the central ledger stays with P7; a refused call is passed to the access-entry writer of RWB-P4-E1039-APP, which P4 owns and which writes no P7 table.
why: DP-03 moves the decision log to a local library plus the shared topic, and the access log is a P4 object that must be written without a P7 table write.
read: Template and Rules §R5.5 DP-03; Ownership Map (decision_log_entry is P7); Architecture v5 slide 14 (access log in rwb_access)
impact: The access query reads the local ledger copy and the central search is P7's operation; a P4 search over a P7 table is not built.

text: The membership refresh interval is five minutes, read from the parameter rwb.access.membership-refresh-minutes=5, so a leaver's session ends at the first request after the refresh.
why: The legacy story assumes the interval (DL38) and no source fixes a value; the parameter keeps it changeable without a build.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-037 section 4 step 11, section 13 and AC8; DL38
impact: A leaver keeps access for at most five minutes after the group is removed; a shorter value costs more group reads, a longer one widens the window.

text: This service keeps the load and approve operations for its own permission and masking tables, while the generic reference-load path for lists, queues, timers, templates and parameters stays with rwb-case.
why: API Specification v4 gives the two operations x-module P4 and TSD P4 v3 T-A names them, while the R-PREC default ruling gives generic reference data to P3; the split is the only reading that keeps both sources.
read: API Specification v4 x-module P4 for /admin/reference-loads and /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve; TSD P4 v3 API-P4-005 and API-P4-006; Template and Rules §R3 default rulings
confirm: Solution architect with the P3 and P4 owners
impact: One gateway route answers two owners unless the two path sets are separated; a merge of the two stories into one owner would move the permission load out of P4.

text: The 756 permission rows of AC1 stand as 54 roles against 14 capability areas, and the roster of TSD P4 v3 T6.1 (42 role codes) grows to 54 by go-live; no row count, role count or area count is a code constant.
why: The legacy criteria count 756 rows and the FSD takes version PM-2026.12 into effect with 756 rows, while the TSD roster lists 42 role codes; the file is the source of the count either way.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-037 AC1 and section 2; FSD P4 A2.1 and A2.4; TSD P4 v3 T6.1
confirm: Security administrator with the solution architect
impact: A version with 42 roles holds 588 rows and fails the legacy count until the roster is completed; the loader must count the file, never a constant.

text: GET /api/recovery/access/v1/masking-policies is the base rule of §R4 applied to the operation Arch v5 slide 14 names, and it answers under Reference data R.
why: Slide 14 names the operation and the service base is fixed by §R4, while the API Specification v4, TSD P4 v3 T-A and the Ownership Map give it no path and no right.
read: Architecture v5 slide 14; Template and Rules §R4 and §R5.5 DP-13; API Specification v4 (no masking-policies path); Ownership Map (no path row)
applied_in: RWB-P4-E1037-CON sections 2 and 12.1; RWB-P4-E1037-APP sections 11 and 12.1
confirm: Solution architect and the API owner
impact: A different path or right breaks the consumer's generated client and needs a new API Specification row; the answer shape is unaffected.

text: rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1 carries the change kind (matrix or masking), the version label, the effective date and the approver reference, and never a field value, a person, a case id or a letter of a role.
why: Arch v5 slide 14 names the event and fixes no payload; the data-minimisation rule of NFR-040 and the no-personal-data rule of slide 35 fix what it may not carry.
read: Architecture v5 slide 14 and slide 35; NFR-040; RWB-PLT-E1037-CON AC3 and AC5
confirm: Solution architect with the event platform owner
impact: A consumer that needs more than the version label must call the matrix read; a richer payload would carry policy data over the topic.

text: The rwb_access baseline objects role, permission, masking_rule, role_conflict and delegation_limit are created by the service template migration V0001 of RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, and this legacy key adds only its two unique indexes, because WP B-P4-01 carries no DB story for RWB-E1-037.
why: The service template owns the schema baseline and every service has its own DB story; this key has none in the WP, so the baseline cannot be left unowned.
read: Template and Rules §R5.5 DP-15 and §R5.7; TSD P4 v3 T3.1; WP B-P4-01 write list (no DB story for RWB-E1-037)
applied_in: RWB-P4-E1037-APP sections 3 and 13; RWB-P4-E1037-CON sections 3 and 12.7
confirm: ACE DB team with the service owner
impact: If the baseline does not carry the five tables, the index migration fails and a DB story of this key must be created before the first load.

text: GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/roles is one path with one contract; RWB-P4-E1019-APP answers the role code, class, default scope and conflict fields and RWB-P4-E1037-APP answers the permission rows and the matrix version of the same answer.
why: The Ownership Map gives P4 one path and the TSD gives it one purpose (list roles with permissions and scope), so two slices contribute fields to one operation instead of publishing two paths.
read: Ownership Map (GET /admin/roles is P4); TSD P4 v3 API-P4-007; API Specification v4 /admin/roles x-module P4; RWB-P4-E1019-APP
confirm: Solution architect with both app owners
impact: Two answers on one path would break the generated client; the merge is at the assembler and one slice must not redefine the other's fields.

text: The policy event is produced through the outbox of the service baseline; DP-09 and RWB-PLT-TE006-CON are not in this legacy key's pattern set or H row, so the delivery guarantee, the retry and the dead-letter topic are the platform event platform's.
why: The WP fixes the pattern set and the H row, and an event cannot be published without the platform's outbox; the baseline carries it for every service.
read: Template and Rules §R5.5 DP-09 and DP-14; WP B-P4-01 story JSON (patterns and H); Architecture v5 slide 20
impact: If the baseline does not carry the outbox, an H dependency on RWB-PLT-TE006-CON must be added to both stories before the event is built.

text: The six-monthly access review list (JOB-18, CTL-10) is a Temporal Schedule on the rwb-access queue owned by RWB-P4-AD008-APP; DP-10 appears in this legacy key only as referred to, and no Schedule, workflow or activity is registered by its stories.
why: Arch v5 slide 14 and slide 44 give the access review Schedule to the access review story, and the WP places it in the sibling; the policy load is an on-demand operation, not a clock.
read: Architecture v5 slide 14 (Temporal Schedule: access review list, six-monthly) and slide 44; legacy RWB-E1-037 section 19; RWB-P4-AD008-APP
applied_in: RWB-P4-E1037-APP sections 3, 12.5 and 19; RWB-P4-E1037-CON sections 12.5 and 19
impact: The workflow-kit dependency is carried on the APP H row for that sibling; if the review belongs elsewhere the H row of RWB-P4-AD008-APP carries it instead.

text: The rwb-case case contract that the criteria call (GET /queues, GET /cases, GET /cases/{caseId}, POST /cases/{caseId}/transfer) is consumed through its published fake only, and the fake is taken as that contract's mock even though WP B-P4-01 carries no C row for it.
why: Rule 4 of the WP requires the cross-service part of a legacy criterion to be expressed as a contract mock, and the only C rows of this WP are the parameters, the reference data and the decision record.
read: Template and Rules §R5.5 DP-11 and §R7.2 s7; WP B-P4-01 story JSON (C row); Ownership Map (GET /queues, GET /cases, POST /cases/{caseId}/transfer are P3)
confirm: Solution architect with the P3 and P4 owners
impact: A build against the fake proves the boundary shape and not the live case service; the live proof is RWB-ITG-E1037-ITG's and the C row can be added there.
